newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to join Zaire intervention force.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to join Zaire intervention force.

text.p: Brazil decided on Thursday to send up to 150 soldiers to join a United Nations intervention force in eastern Zaire, a spokesman for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said.

Spokesman Sergio Amaral said between 120 and 150 soldiers would be sent from Angola, where Brazilian troops are taking part in a U.N.-sponsored peace operation. He said no date had yet been set for the Brazilian soldiers to travel to Zaire.
Earlier, the Foreign Ministry said Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, whose country will take the lead in the operation, had asked Cardoso to contribute to the force.
"The president of the republic reacted favourably to the request for a Brazilian contribution," the ministry said.

Gen. Alberto Cardoso, the senior military officer in the Presidential Palace, said in a briefing with foreign journalists late on Wednesday that Brazil would not "shirk its responsibilities if asked to help out."
"(In Zaire) genocide is taking place. President Cardoso is very shocked by what is happening," he said.

The general, noting Brazilian peacekeeping experience under U.N. auspices in Mozambique and Angola, said Brasilia envisaged more active participation in international peacekeeping following the introduction of a new National Defence Policy. "One of the objectives of the (new) policy is the projection of the country abroad," he said.
